title: Detect Cycles in 2D Grid
summary: In a grid of characters, determine if there is a cycle of the same value where a cycle is defined as a path of at least four cells starting and ending at the same cell, moving only to adjacent cells with the same value, and not revisiting the last cell immediately.
statement: In a grid of characters, determine if there is a cycle of the same value where a cycle is defined as a path of at least four cells starting and ending at the same cell, moving only to adjacent cells with the same value, and not revisiting the last cell immediately.
constraints: Move orthogonally between cells containing the same character.
Return whether a path of at least four distinct cells can return to its start without immediately reversing an edge.
hints: Run DFS within each same-character component.
Pass the immediately previous cell so its undirected edge is ignored.
Encountering any other already visited same-character neighbor proves a cycle.
A simple orthogonal grid has no triangles, so every such undirected cycle has at least four cells.
editorial: A simple orthogonal grid has no triangles, so every such undirected cycle has at least four cells.

tests.explanation: The outer ring of a cells forms a cycle.
